paper_title: Extremal Combinatorics, Iterated Pigeonhole Arguments and Generalizations of PPP
statement: The generalizations of PPP which we explore in this paper seem to give rise to a remarkably rich set of tantalizing open questions. Some examples: 1. Prove black box separations between the problems and classes studied in this paper. For example, prove a separation between PPP and PLC; between PEPP and PSC; between PPP and the hierarchy of Turán and Bad coloring problems. 2. What other natural problems belong to PLC or are PLC-complete? One problem in TFNP that has long evaded classification is Bertrand-Chebyshev: given a number n, find a prime number between n and 2n. 3. What is the complexity of finding monochromatic cliques in smaller graphs, whose existence is guaranteed by a century of fascinating improvements of Ramsey’s theorem? 4. What natural problems belong to the class PSC (but not to PEPP)? 5. How does PLC relate to problems in cryptography, and specifically lattices? 6. The Bad Coloring hierarchy suggests a novel source of computational hardness: inefficient encoding of objects. What other interesting natural problems share this type of hardness? 7. More generally, what other problems from extremal combinatorics give rise to search problems in TFNP, and how are these problems classified in TFNP subclasses?
